name: Hyperlink ping attribute
plain: A link attribute that makes the browser send a POST to extra URLs when the link is clicked.
meaning: Lets a site or ad network count clicks without a redirect or script. Body is the text PING, with Ping-From and Ping-To headers. Firefox ships it disabled by default, and blockers and Brave drop it.

access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can tell extra web addresses when you click a link, without you noticing
limits.user_action: You click a link that has a ping address attached
can: Send a small message to extra addresses the moment you click
Report which link you clicked and which page you were on
Work even when the link opens a new page right away
cannot: Run unless you click that specific link
See what you do after the click on the next site
Work in Firefox by default, where it is switched off
Show a prompt or any sign that it happened
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge, Safari and Samsung Internet send it. Firefox has it turned off by default.

story.what_it_is: A link tag that makes the browser quietly tell another address when you click the link.

marketing.name: a ping attribute
marketing.pitch: Developer docs describe ping as a list of addresses that get a short POST when a link is followed.

story.for_you: You click a link and go where you expected. You do not see that a tiny note was sent to a counting server as you left. It only happens in browsers that allow it, and Firefox keeps it off by default.
story.for_makers: It lets a site count clicks with no redirect and no script, so the link feels fast. Search and ad systems like it for outbound click counts. It is easy for blockers to drop, so makers trust it less than scripts.

use_cases.example: You click a sponsored result and the browser pings the ad system to count the click, while you go straight to the advertiser page.
A news site counts how many readers click out to a partner article without adding any slow redirect.
A coupon site counts clicks to each store link so it can bill stores for traffic.
A forum counts outbound clicks on shared links to show which posts send people away.
A game portal counts clicks on Play now links to partner game sites, so it can pay a revenue share.
A security team can spot odd ping targets in a page, which is a sign a link is being used for hidden counting.

risks: Not blockable by the person without a setting

technical_bounds: Only on link clicks, not on form submit
Cookies for the ping origin are sent
